item.title: Chair of Rowing Ireland refuses to apologise to athletes including Kerry rower, over treatment in high performance programme
item.description: The Chair of Rowing Ireland has refused to apologise to athletes, including Kerry’s Monika Dukarska, for what he described as unacceptable experiences in their high performance programme. Barry McWilliams was one of three Rowing Ireland representatives who came before an Oireachtas hearing today, along with representatives from Sport Ireland. The meeting had been called following revelations in the Sunday Independent in November about allegations of mistreatment in the high performance programme

item.title: Calls for bus services at Kerry Airport to be coordinated with plane departures and arrivals
item.description: A Kerry County Councillor is calling for bus services at Kerry Airport to be coordinated with scheduled plane departure and arrival times. Councillor John O'Donoghue made the call at the recent full council meeting. The Kerry Independent Alliance councillor believes the bus service currently does not tie in well with plane departure times. item.title: Auction date set for sale of former Kerry garda station which closed in 2013
item.description: A former garda station in Kerry will be sold at auction next month, 13 years after it closed. Estate agents ERA Downey McCarthy are bringing the former Brosna garda station to the market by public auction. Advertisement The station closed in January 2013, and was then transferred to the Office of Public Works which has owned it since. item.title: Council urged to install tide clocks on popular North Kerry beach
item.description: Kerry County Council has been urged to install tide clocks on the Ladies Beach in Ballybunion. Fine Gael councillor, Aoife Kennelly tabled the motion at the recent Listowel MD meeting. She says locals are aware of how quickly the tide can change here, and having tidal clocks on the beach are a practical option to make the beach safer. item.title: Planning granted for demolition of all structures at Tralee racecourse
item.description: Planning has been granted for the demolition of all existing structures at the former Tralee racecourse. Ard Rí Marble purchased the 100-acre Ballybeggan site in 2024 for a price understood to be around €5 million, with plans for warehousing, manufacturing, and potentially housing for staff. Advertisement It has now been granted permission to demolish all buildings including the two landmark stands, one of which is said to date back to the early 20th century.
